survey: A red K6-style telephone box, seen three-quarter from the front-left. Main parts: (1) A purple plinth that the whole box stands on flat. (2) Four corner posts holding up a cornice band. The cornice carries a domed roof with an arched pediment on each face. Each pediment has a gold crown and a blank cream sign panel. The front crown faces the camera; the side crown is turned away at an angle. (3) The left side wall is a fixed glazed panel of 3×5 panes in a red frame. (4) The front face is a glazed door in the frame between the front corner posts. It has a yellow pull handle on its right edge, fixed by two stand-offs to the right stile and glazing bar. (5) A blue payphone with a keypad, screen and handset on a hook. Its coiled cord loops from the base to the handset. It should be mounted inside the box and seen through the door glass. The plinth sits on the ground and casts a shadow, and the roof, posts and walls all join up. The one fault is how the phone sits against the door glazing.

errors.where: Front door, centre: the payphone and the glazing bars around it
errors.what: The payphone is drawn over the door's window grid instead of behind it. The middle column of the door has no horizontal glazing bar where the phone is, though the bars carry on in the narrow side columns. The phone and its coiled cord are not behind the glass, so the phone reads as stuck to the outside of the door, or as having broken through the glazing. It does not look like a phone on the back wall seen through the panes.

fix: Keep the door's window grid whole: every horizontal and vertical glazing bar runs across the full door, including the centre column. Mount the blue payphone on the back wall inside the telephone box, seen through the glass behind the red glazing bars. The bars cross in front of the phone, and the phone and cord are slightly tinted by the glass.
